name: hkx-gan-pass
description: Single generator-evaluator pass for a GAN-style build loop: the generator implements or improves the artifact against gan/spec.md, then an isolated read-only evaluator tests the running result and returns scores plus a pass/fail/plateau/blocked verdict. The main loop owns repetition and the stop decision.

chain.label: Implement or improve the artifact
chain.task:
Run one generator iteration for this build.

Brief:
{task}

Read `gan/spec.md` first — it is the contract for what done means. If `gan/feedback.md` exists, read it and address every finding in this iteration, ordered by functionality defects first, then robustness, craft, omitted features, and design.

First iteration: scaffold per the spec's technical constraints, implement the must-have features end to end enough to be runnable, start the runbook from the spec's "How to run it" section, then smoke-check.
Later iteration: fix the feedback, re-run the runbook, and verify each named issue is actually gone.

You are the only writer in this worktree. Do not self-evaluate and do not produce rubric scores — that judgment belongs to the evaluator. Do not edit the spec or rubric, do not weaken or delete tests, and do not leave the build in a non-runnable state.

Write `gan/generator-state.md` (what was built, how to run it, feedback addressed vs outstanding, known gaps, commands run) and return: iteration number, file-level changes, runbook status with URL if relevant, issues addressed vs outstanding, and anything the parent must decide.

chain.label: Score the running artifact
chain.task:
Evaluate the running artifact for this build.

Brief:
{task}

Generator report for this iteration:
{outputs.gen}

Read `gan/spec.md` first, especially its "How to run it" section. Then establish the evaluation mode you can actually achieve (live / headless / static) and state it explicitly — a runbook failure is a `blocked` verdict, never a silent downgrade to a static code read scored as if it were live.

Test the artifact, not the author's summary: run the runbook verbatim, walk every numbered must-have feature on the happy path plus edge cases (empty, oversized, unicode, double submit, refresh mid-flow), probe error states, and audit cross-artifact consistency. Score Functionality/Craft/Coherence/Robustness 1-10 against the weighted rubric (pass threshold 7.0) unless the spec supplies its own criteria.

You have no write tools — findings go in your report. Never suggest a fix and then grade it. Every must-fix needs evidence: a command you ran, a path and line, or a reproduced behavior. Requirements absent from the spec go under `Spec Gaps`, not under must-fix.

Return the report (mode, runbook, score table with arithmetic, must-fix, should-fix, nitpicks, spec gaps) ending with exactly one verdict: pass | fail | plateau | blocked, and one paragraph justifying it.
